item.title: Music Beneath the Radio Calls

turns.text: Add a tense instrumental bed to this. Keep it under the radio calls so every word is easy to hear, especially 'Rook, you with me?' Don't change the footage.

item.tests: Tests whether added music remains audibly subordinate to the original speech, with intelligibility preserved throughout the delivered video.

answer_sheet.Music mood and vocals: Tense instrumental music, with no singing.
answer_sheet.Music level relative to speech: Clearly quieter than the radio calls whenever someone speaks; every original word must remain easy to hear.
answer_sheet.Source footage, duration, and framing: Keep the entire attached 7-second cockpit clip, with unchanged visuals, timing, and framing.
answer_sheet.Speech and added text: Keep the original radio-call recording in sync. Do not replace it or add text.

must_haves: The output preserves all seven seconds of the original cockpit footage without visual changes or extra shots.
A tense instrumental music bed is audible, with no added singing.
The original radio calls remain present and synchronized, including the clearly intelligible line 'Rook, you with me?'
During every spoken line, the music is perceptibly below the voice and does not mask words with loud beats, swells, or accents.
The music is not simply muted for the entire clip; it is audible while remaining subordinate to speech.

turns.text: Add a tense instrumental bed to the attached clip. Keep it under the radio calls so every word is easy to hear, especially “Rook, you with me?” Don’t change the footage. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do this?

dialog.agent:
**Nothing has run or spent credits.** To preserve the footage and radio calls, this needs an audio-only mix—not video generation.

**Cost and lower-cost options**
- **Generate a tense instrumental:** 1 credit per requested second, with a **15-second minimum = 15 credits**. A 30-second track costs 30 credits. I haven’t verified your available balance.
- **Cheaper:** use a licensed track you already have, or a royalty-free track whose license covers your use: **0 Magic Hour generation credits**.
- **Shorter:** generate 15 seconds, then trim or loop it in an editor. Requesting less than 15 seconds won’t reduce the generation minimum.
- **Smaller:** lowering the video resolution won’t reduce music-generation cost—and isn’t necessary.

For clarity, I’d use sparse, tense music without vocals, lower it during all radio calls, and dip it further around **“Rook, you with me?”** The final level needs checking against the actual dialogue.

**Limitation:** the connected tools can generate music, but don’t expose a way to mix it under this existing clip with dialogue ducking while leaving the footage untouched. That step would need an editor such as DaVinci Resolve or Shotcut.

How long is the clip, and would you prefer the **zero-credit existing-track route** or a **15-credit, 15-second generated bed**? I’ll wait for your approval before generating anything.
dialog.user: The clip is 7 seconds; keep all of it with the visuals and original radio calls unchanged and in sync. For the zero-credit route, ok, go ahead with that.

dialog.agent:
Understood: keep all **7 seconds**, with the visuals and original radio calls unchanged and in sync. **No credits have been spent.**

I can’t complete the zero-credit mix through the connected tools: they don’t provide audio mixing, and there isn’t an existing music track attached.

To do this free in Shotcut or DaVinci Resolve:
1. Keep the original clip and its audio untouched.
2. Add a licensed tense instrumental on a separate audio track, trimmed to 7 seconds.
3. Start the music roughly **20–25 dB below the dialogue**, then lower it further during radio calls—especially **“Rook, you with me?”**
4. Export the full 7 seconds at the original frame rate and dimensions.

Use a royalty-free track whose license covers your intended use. That route costs **0 Magic Hour credits**; I won’t run a generation as a substitute.
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with the cheapest option you listed

dialog.agent:
The cheapest option is still **0 Magic Hour credits**: use an existing licensed instrumental and mix it in a free editor.

I can’t execute that mix with the connected tools, and no music track is attached. **Nothing has run or spent credits.** I won’t switch you to paid generation.

Do you have a licensed instrumental to use, and are you working in **Shotcut or DaVinci Resolve**? I can give you exact steps to keep all 7 seconds, preserve the footage and radio-call timing, and lower the music around “Rook, you with me?”
dialog.user: I haven’t specified a music track or editor; the instrumental style is your call, as long as it’s tense with no singing. Keep the route free and preserve all 7 seconds and every radio-call word.

turns.agent:
I’d choose a **sparse, low synth drone with a slow pulse—tense, no vocals, and no sharp hits that compete with the radio calls**.

But I can’t complete the free mix here: the connected tools neither supply free stock music nor mix audio into an existing clip. Generating music would cost at least **15 credits**, so I won’t run that.

The zero-credit route requires an external editor and a free licensed track. Keep the original 7-second clip and audio untouched, add the music separately, and duck only the music during every call—especially **“Rook, you with me?”** Then check the full mix for intelligibility before exporting.

**Nothing has been generated, changed, or charged.**
